structured_output.strongest_bear_case: The activity looks manufactured by micro-trade bots, not real demand. In the first hour about 20.5k trades produced only about $147k in volume, roughly $7 per trade. A live DexScreener check shortly after detection showed about 2,514 trades for $5.9k over five minutes, about $2.30 per trade. Unique buyers (3,032) and unique sellers (3,007) are nearly equal and close to the holder count (3,085), which fits a pool of wallets buying and selling tiny amounts to inflate trade and holder counts. RugCheck's only warning, a very high market cap relative to holder count, fits this. The price has already peaked and reversed: GeckoTerminal shows -45.6% over 30 minutes and -22.6% over the hour, and the +1,192% figure is measured from the launch price. The token also borrows an identity it doesn't own. Its only social link is Sony's official @SpiderManMovie account, there is no website, Telegram or DexScreener profile, and the description is a throwaway line. It is one of about 10 same-name pump.fun launches in the past day, and the other nine are all dead at $2–5k market cap. I found no fresh Spider-Man news on 2026-09-21 to explain the spike: Brand New Day released in the summer, and the only upcoming items are a Disney+ Halloween special (Sept 25), a Spider-Noir TV rating and a New York Comic Con reveal. The structure itself is clean (mint and freeze authority renounced, liquidity pool locked, top 10 hold 15.5%), so the risk is fading attention and recycled volume, not a rug.
